issues.legal_issue: A bidder does not breach the published terms of an auction by refusing material conditions added only after the bid is accepted, or by stopping payment after the authority adds those conditions, where the bidder tendered the required initial payment by a method the authority accepted.
material_facts: The auction notice required a security deposit and an immediate payment of one-fourth of the accepted bid, but did not state the additional lease-rent conditions later imposed.
The bidder deposited the required one-fourth payment by cheque on the day of the auction, and the authority accepted the cheque.
After accepting the bid, the authority sent the bidder additional lease conditions that had not been included in the auction notice or communicated before the auction.
The bidder refused the additional conditions and stopped payment of the cheque after receiving them.
issues.conclusion: The additional conditions were not binding on the bidder, who was entitled to withdraw from the auction; the bidder did not breach the published auction terms by stopping payment after those conditions were imposed.
issues.legal_principle: A contracting party may insist only on terms that form part of the contract and may not unilaterally add or alter terms without the other party’s consent. Material auction terms must be disclosed to bidders when bids are invited; undisclosed terms cannot be enforced against a bidder. The Court also relied on the accepted cheque as compliance with the payment term.

rule.if: public_auction_contract_dispute and material_terms_not_disclosed and terms_added_after_bid_acceptance and required_payment_tendered_by_accepted_method and bidder_rejected_added_terms

predicates.public_auction_contract_dispute: The dispute concerns a bidder’s obligations under a public auction and the authority’s treatment of the bidder’s security deposit.
predicates.material_terms_not_disclosed: The authority did not include material payment or lease conditions in the published auction terms or otherwise disclose them to bidders before bidding.
predicates.terms_added_after_bid_acceptance: The authority communicated additional contractual conditions to the bidder only after accepting the bid.
predicates.required_payment_tendered_by_accepted_me: The bidder tendered the required payment by a method that the authority accepted.
predicates.bidder_rejected_added_terms: The bidder refused to accept the additional conditions imposed after the bid was accepted.

issues.definition: When an auction authority leaves material conditions undisclosed, adds them after accepting a bid, and the bidder tendered the required payment by an accepted method but rejects the additions, the bidder has not breached the published auction terms.

issues.legal_issue: An authority cannot forfeit a security deposit for breach of an auction contract unless the contract contains a stipulation granting a right of forfeiture.
material_facts: The auction notice required bidders to deposit security but contained no term authorizing forfeiture or specifying the circumstances in which forfeiture could occur.
The authority relied on provisions said to be part of a revenue circular, but the auction notice did not state that the circular governed the auction or reproduce the relevant provisions.
The authority forfeited the bidder’s security deposit after the bidder refused conditions added after acceptance of the bid.
issues.conclusion: The authority had no right to forfeit the security deposit because the auction terms contained no stipulation authorizing forfeiture.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, forfeiture of earnest money or security requires a contractual stipulation authorizing it. A right to forfeit is contractual and penal in nature. The Court distinguished Maula Bux v. Union of India, 1969(2) SCC 354, and Shri Hanuman Cotton Mills v. Tata Air Craft Ltd., 1969(3) SCC 522, because those contracts contained specific forfeiture clauses. It relied on Union of India v. Vertex Broadcasting Company Private Limited, (2015) 16 SCC 198, which held forfeiture illegal in the absence of contractual power to forfeit.

predicates.security_forfeiture_dispute: The dispute concerns an authority’s forfeiture of a bidder’s security deposit in an auction contract.
predicates.no_express_forfeiture_term: The contract terms did not expressly grant the authority a right to forfeit the security deposit.

issues.definition: In a dispute over an authority’s forfeiture of auction security, if the contract contains no express forfeiture term, the authority has no right to forfeit the security.

issues.legal_issue: Forfeiture of a bidder’s security is unjustified where the authority suffers no monetary loss from the bidder’s withdrawal and a re-auction of the property yields more than the bidder’s offer.
material_facts: After the auction was cancelled, the authority re-auctioned the plot for an amount substantially higher than the bidder’s offer.
The authority did not dispute that the re-auction produced the higher amount.
The Court found that the authority suffered no monetary loss in the transaction.
issues.conclusion: The absence of monetary loss, together with the higher amount obtained at re-auction, was an additional reason why forfeiting the security deposit was wholly unjustified.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the lack of monetary loss in the circumstances of this case as an additional ground against forfeiture, alongside its conclusion that the contract contained no forfeiture right. Section 74 of the Indian Contract Act, 1872, provides for reasonable compensation for breach, subject to the stipulated maximum; the Court relied on the absence of loss here as an additional reason, not as a general rule that proof of loss is always necessary for relief under that section.

rule.if: public_auction_contract_dispute and security_forfeited and reauction_yielded_more_than_bid and authority_suffered_no_monetary_loss

predicates.public_auction_contract_dispute: The dispute concerns security forfeited after a bidder withdrew from a public auction transaction.
predicates.security_forfeited: The authority retained or confiscated the bidder’s security deposit.
predicates.reauction_yielded_more_than_bid: The authority later re-auctioned the property for more than the withdrawing bidder had offered.
predicates.authority_suffered_no_monetary_loss: The authority suffered no monetary loss from the transaction after the re-auction.

issues.definition: When an authority forfeits auction security, but a re-auction yields more than the bidder’s offer and the authority suffers no monetary loss, the forfeiture is unjustified.
